stories.title: World Series Game 1 — Brewers vs Rays, Friday Oct 23 at American Family Field

x_posts.label: Post 1
x_posts.text:
The Fall Classic is here.

Brewers vs Rays — Game 1
Friday | Oct 23 | 8:07 PM ET | FOX | American Family Field

Two No. 1 seeds. Zero World Series titles between them.
One of them ends that drought in October 2026.

#WorldSeries #MILvsTB #MLB

facebook.long_form:
The Fall Classic is two days away.

Game 1 of the 2026 World Series goes Friday night at American Family Field in Milwaukee — first pitch 8:07 PM ET, broadcast on FOX.

For the first time in baseball history, two No. 1 seeds are meeting in the Fall Classic, and neither franchise has ever won a World Series title. The Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays are both chasing history.

These clubs are mirror images of each other in almost every way. Both built on contact hitting, elite defense, aggressive baserunning, and dominant bullpens. Both are masterclasses in analytical roster construction. And both are completely capable of beating anyone in baseball.

The Brewers went 4-0 at home in the 2026 playoffs. The Rays went 3-1 at home. Whoever wins the home games likely wins this series.

Vegas opened with Milwaukee as -160 favorites, Tampa Bay at +140. But any gambler who followed this Rays team all season knows those numbers tell only part of the story.

Game 1: Friday, October 23. 8:07 PM ET. FOX. One of the greatest Fall Classic setups in years. ⚾

article.headline: World Series 2026: Brewers vs. Rays, Two No. 1 Seeds Chasing History

stories.title: Jacob Misiorowski's Workload Question Heading Into the Fall Classic

x_posts.label: Post 2
x_posts.text:
Jacob Misiorowski this season:

21-8 record
2.51 ERA (MLB leader)
339 Ks
Arm fatigue managed all July

Now he's getting 4-4.5 innings per WS start.
His bullpen has a 0.38 ERA this postseason.

Milwaukee built the perfect machine around him.

#Brewers #WorldSeries #MLB

facebook.long_form:
Jacob Misiorowski is the best pitcher in baseball. And heading into the World Series, his workload is the most important question Milwaukee faces.

The 2026 numbers are staggering: 21-8, 2.51 ERA, 339 strikeouts — the MLB leader in both categories. A two-time All-Star who spent his July managing arm fatigue, then came back and kept his ERA and strikeout totals as the best in the majors.

The caution has followed him into October. Misiorowski has been averaging just 4-4.5 innings per postseason start. The Brewers aren't pushing him. And why would they? Their bullpen has posted a 0.38 ERA through 23.2 innings in the 2026 playoffs — one of the most dominant relief performances in postseason history.

So the real question isn't whether Misiorowski is healthy. It's whether Milwaukee's October formula — elite starter plus elite bullpen — can hold up through a seven-game series against Tampa Bay's patient, contact-heavy offense.

If it can, the Brewers win the championship. If the Rays can grind starters and bullpens deeper into the lineup, they flip the script.

Game 1 starts Friday. 🍺

article.headline: The Misiorowski Question: How Deep Can Milwaukee Push Its Ace in the World Series?

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
Everyone's talking about Misiorowski.

The Brewers bullpen quietly has a 0.38 ERA in 23.2 postseason innings.

DL Hall: 8.2 IP, 0 runs
Aaron Ashby: 12.1 shutout IP
Uribe: sub-2.00 ERA two straight seasons

4th best postseason ERA in Wild Card era.

#Brewers #WorldSeries #MLB

facebook.long_form:
The national conversation about the Brewers has been dominated by Jacob Misiorowski. Fair enough — he's the NL Cy Young frontrunner.

But Milwaukee's real secret weapon this October has been the bullpen.

Through the NLCS, the Brewers' relief corps posted a 0.38 ERA in 23.2 innings — the 4th best postseason bullpen ERA in the Wild Card era. Numbers that belong in the history books.

The breakdown: DL Hall has thrown 8.2 innings in the 2026 playoffs without allowing a single run. Aaron Ashby has logged 12.1 shutout innings in postseason play. Thyago Uribe has posted a sub-2.00 ERA in each of the last two regular seasons and is the primary setup bridge. Devin Megill closes out games.

What makes this unit so important is the role it plays alongside Misiorowski. With the ace averaging only 4-4.5 innings per start, the bullpen is responsible for more than half of every game. And they've been perfect.

The Rays can't just wait out Misiorowski to get to a vulnerable Milwaukee bullpen. There is no vulnerable Milwaukee bullpen.

article.headline: The Brewers' Best-Kept Secret: A Bullpen With a 0.38 ERA in the Playoffs

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
Don't overlook Junior Caminero this World Series.

2025: 45 HR, 110 RBI
2026 ALCS G6: 2-run HR off the foul pole
Two-time All-Star

A slow 2026 regular season doesn't define him.
He is Tampa Bay's most dangerous bat. 🔥

#Rays #WorldSeries #MLB

facebook.long_form:
If the Tampa Bay Rays are going to win the 2026 World Series, Junior Caminero may be the reason why.

Two years ago, Caminero announced himself on the national stage with a 2025 season for the ages: 45 home runs, 110 RBI, a first All-Star selection, and a second-place MVP finish. He entered 2026 as one of baseball's most feared bats.

Then a slow start and an injury limited him to 51 regular season games. The counting numbers — .265/.356/.490, 13 home runs, 27 RBI — didn't reflect the player he'd become. A lot of teams wrote him off as diminished.

The ALCS changed that narrative in one swing.

With the Rays facing elimination in Game 6, Caminero put a 2-run home run off the foul pole. Not a cheap shot — an absolute bullet that went exactly where he intended. Tampa Bay survived. And suddenly opposing pitchers were no longer treating him as a problem they'd solved.

He's healthy, he's locked in, and he's earned Milwaukee's full attention. The Brewers' pitching plan for Game 1 almost certainly starts with a simple question: how do we handle Caminero?
facebook.image_caption: ALCS Game 6. Caminero off the foul pole. Tampa Bay's most dangerous bat is ready for the World Series. #Rays #WorldSeries #MLB

article.headline: Junior Caminero Is Tampa Bay's X-Factor — and Milwaukee Knows It

stories.title: Drew Rasmussen's Historic October — Probable Game 1 WS Starter

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
Drew Rasmussen's 2026 postseason:

1.29 ERA across 15 innings
Near no-hitter through 6+ innings vs Yankees in ALDS
10 Ks, 1-0 win in Game 1

He's the most dominant pitcher in this October.
Now he gets Game 1 of the World Series. #Rays #WorldSeries #MLB

facebook.long_form:
Drew Rasmussen is the most dominant pitcher in the 2026 postseason — and he's starting Game 1 of the World Series.

The regular season résumé is excellent: 16-5, 2.67 ERA, two All-Star selections. But it's what he's done in October that sets him apart from anyone else in either dugout.

In ALDS Game 1 against the Yankees, Rasmussen was nearly untouchable. He carried a no-hitter through more than six innings, finished with 10 strikeouts, and left with the Rays winning 1-0. That performance set the tone for Tampa Bay's entire run.

Through 15 total innings in the 2026 playoffs, Rasmussen has posted a 1.29 ERA. He hasn't just been good — he's been the kind of dominant that October legends are made of.

Now comes the biggest game of his career. American Family Field, Friday night, with the World Series on the line. The Brewers' lineup will be the toughest test yet. But if Rasmussen pitches anything like he did against the Yankees, this could be a long night for Milwaukee.

Game 2 probables: Framber Peralta for Tampa Bay against Milwaukee's Shintaro Henderson. But first, it's Rasmussen on Friday. ⚾
